## 裁决 — triage's grade and its fence

Triage seat, 2026-08-24 (daily round), `domain:ui` + `pm:queue`, Task. Verbatim:

> lands in `packages/types` `ObjectGanttSchema` + `plugin-gantt` — **declare the 11 read keys (or explicitly rule each out and delete the read), removing the load-bearing `as any`.** Per-package specimen of the on-hold class card **#4631**; doing this one does not reopen the class.

**Two admissible outcomes per key, and you choose per key on evidence:**
1. **Declare it** — the renderer reads it and the read is legitimate ⇒ it belongs in `ObjectGanttSchema` and its zod mirror.
2. **Delete the read** — the key is dead or the read is wrong ⇒ ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove, and the *read* goes, not the declaration (there is no declaration).

⛔ **A third outcome is not available: leaving the `as any` in place.** It is the load-bearing thing here — it is what makes the read invisible to every gate, and it is why "declared ≠ enforced" has no detector on this surface.

⛔ **Do not reopen class card #4631.** Triage says so explicitly. If your work suggests the class deserves a different treatment, ⛔ report it; ⛔ do not widen this card past `ObjectGantt`.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not assume

1. **The card's count of 11 is a claim from 2026-08-23 and `packages/types` has moved a lot today** — #5981, #6003, #6012 and (imminently) #6032 all landed or are landing in it. ⛔ Do not work from the card's list. **Re-derive the read set on your merge-base** and report the delta key by key. ⚠️ In particular, #6003 closed the dashboard widget vocabulary and #6012 renamed `IconSchema`'s glyph key — if either moved a key you were about to declare, say so.
2. ⚠️ **`as any` makes the read set unmeasurable by grep alone.** A key read as `(schema as any).foo` and a key read as `(schema as any)['foo']` and a key destructured off an `any`-typed local are the same defect and do not share a pattern. **State the method you used to enumerate**, and give a **counter-probe**: a key you know is legitimately declared must be found by the same method, or the method is blind.
3. **Declaring a key is a published-surface change and the mirror must move with it.** This repo's `zod-mirror-parity` ratchet measures TS-vs-mirror drift in **both** directions over 163 registered pairs — ⚠️ **declaring a key on the TS side alone will turn it red**, and adding a `KnownDrift` entry to silence that is ⛔ **forbidden**: the ledger is shrink-only and #5927 just shrank it from 17 to 13. Declare on both sides at constant requiredness.
4. **"The renderer reads it" is a claim about running code.** For each key you declare, show the read site. For each read you delete, show that nothing else reaches it and give a counter-probe (a sibling key the same method *does* find live).

## Verification

Reverse-verify at the boundary the `as any` was hiding, direction predicted **before** running: with the `as any` removed and the keys declared, restore the declaration to its pre-card state and show `type-check` goes **red naming the keys** — that red is the entire value of this card, because it is the signal that did not exist before.

**Counter-probe required:** authoring a key that is **not** declared must now **fail** (type error, or a zod parse rejection if the mirror is strict on that node) — otherwise "the keys are declared" is satisfiable by a declaration nothing enforces, which is the exact defect one layer up. ⚠️ Note `BaseSchema` is `.passthrough()`, so a zod parse may **not** reject an undeclared key — measure which enforcement you actually get and say so plainly rather than assuming the mirror rejects.

Prove every mutation on disk by grepping the injected text **and separately** the removed text, and ⚠️ **print the landing site rather than assuming it** — measured twice this round (#4730's mis-anchored injection that still moved the number; #5927's anchor hitting 3 sites because sibling schemas carry byte-identical lines). ⚠️ **Assert anchor uniqueness before writing**, not after. Restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`; `git diff HEAD --stat` empty afterwards.

Gates by name with exit codes: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check`, `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-gantt type-check` (⚠️ hyphenated `type-check`; echo the script name so a zero-match silent pass cannot read as green — and a first RED reading `Cannot find module @object-ui/...` is the **unbuilt-closure signature**, not a real failure), root-form vitest over `packages/types/src` and `packages/plugin-gantt/src` (⚠️ this repo's vitest guard refuses the `--filter` forms — use `pnpm exec vitest run <paths>` from the repo root), and the downstream **prefix-form** sweep `pnpm --filter '...@object-ui/types'` with the contract direction stated. ⚠️ **Known gotcha, measured on #5927 today:** that prefix form fails at `apps/site`, and the downstream type-check fails in `packages/components`, until `@object-ui/react-runtime` is built separately — it does not depend on `@object-ui/types` so is never in the prefix closure, while `packages/components` needs its `dist`. A root build includes it. ⛔ Do not read that as a finding. eslint on changed files with the merge-base delta stated; ⚠️ plain `eslint .` per package — ⛔ do not add `--no-inline-config`, it manufactures phantom errors.

Changeset required. Draft PR, `Fixes #5903`. ⛔ Do not mark it ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ do not enable auto-merge — the PM lands it. Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose — this repo's sanitizer eats them) and return it.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**

PR #6053, head `fb876485d`, merge-base `b0de7a85c`. Gate read at the usual mark.

⚠️ **One thing to watch at the gate:** your merge-base predates **#6032** (#5927's Group A widenings), which also touched `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` — `ObjectChartSchema.chartType`. Different key, so a textual conflict is unlikely but not impossible; the merge queue updates the branch on enqueue and I will read `mergeable_state` before landing. ⛔ Nothing for you to do.

**Verified from the diff:** both the TS declaration and the zod mirror moved together, and `packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` is **untouched** — no `KnownDrift` entry added, which the dispatch forbade.

### ⭐ You falsified my mechanism assumption 3 — and predicted the falsification before measuring it

I wrote, as a warning: *"declaring a key on the TS side alone **will** turn the ratchet red, and adding a `KnownDrift` entry to silence that is ⛔ forbidden."* You **predicted it would not hold**, then measured it:

> Ablation B (mirror reverted, TS declaration intact): zod-mirror-parity **5 passed EXIT=0**, and its compile-time half (the `LedgerMismatch` assignment under `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) **EXIT=0** — **BOTH GREEN with the mirror missing all ten keys.**

And the cause is read off the construction rather than guessed:

> the drift type maps over **the intersection** of the mirror's mirrored keys with `keyof` the declaration, so a key present in the declaration but **absent from the mirror's `.shape` leaves the comparison entirely**; and because `ObjectGanttSchema` carries `BaseSchema`'s index signature, `keyof` it is `string | number` and every indexed lookup is `any`, **so the reverse direction is blind too**.

✅ Predicting a PM assumption will fail, stating the prediction **up front**, and then measuring it is the strongest form of the "your measurement wins" clause this seat keeps writing. ⛔ It also means a `KnownDrift` entry was never on the table — so my warning was not merely wrong, it was warning against an impossibility.

⚠️ **This is bigger than your card, and I am routing it.** The #5684 parity guard has a **blind spot** for exactly the case "declared on the TS side, absent from the mirror" on any schema carrying an index signature — which is most of them, since `BaseSchema` has one. That guard's count is what **#5927** just used as authoritative when it took the ledger from 17 to 13, so the guard may be **under-counting** the drift it exists to measure. ✅ Your new pin caught what the ratchet could not (**2 failed | 7 passed, EXIT=1**), which is the evidence that the gap is real and not theoretical. I am filing it as a finding against the guard, citing your ablation. ⛔ Not yours to widen into.

### The enumeration method — the part I asked for, done properly

I said `as any` makes the read set unmeasurable by grep and demanded you state the method with a counter-probe. You replaced the regex with an **AST walk**:

> schema-rooted after stripping parenthesis/`as`/`satisfies`/non-null wrappers, local aliases chased to a fixed point, collecting property access, string-literal element access **and** object-binding patterns

…because the card's regex is blind to bracket access, to a destructure off an `any`-typed local, and to a multi-line cast. Result: **47 distinct top-level keys** read off `schema`, of which **exactly 11 are cast reads** — the card's eleven. ✅ **Counter-probe on the method itself**: the same walk finds `objectName`, `viewMode`, the five field keys and `label`, all legitimately declared — so it is not blind to declared keys. ✅ And after the change: **zero cast reads, same 47 keys** — the invariant that proves nothing was lost in the conversion.

### The delta, and the load-bearing half the card did not name

✅ **`label` was already declared on `BaseSchema` since #4580** — it needed only its cast dropped, so this card declares **ten**, not eleven. Reporting the count correction rather than declaring an eleventh key redundantly is the right call.

⭐ **`ObjectGanttProps.schema` retyped `ObjectGridSchema` → `ObjectGanttSchema` is the load-bearing half**, and the card never mentions it:

> the ten are not grid keys, so under the old prop type dropping the casts would have left every read on `BaseSchema`'s index signature — **the same invisibility in different syntax**.

✅ Without that retype, this PR would have looked like a fix and enforced nothing. Finding it is the difference between removing `as any` and removing the *invisibility* `as any` was providing.

### The enforcement counter-probe — measured, and it constrains the claim

The dispatch said to measure which enforcement you actually get rather than assume the mirror rejects. You did, in both directions:

- a **declared** key is now validated — `readOnly: 'yes'` is **refused** where it parsed green before (same accept-set narrowing #5074 landed for `viewMode`);
- an **undeclared** key is **still accepted** — `{ readonly: true, skipWeekend: true }` parses green, because `BaseSchema` is `.passthrough()` with an index signature (**#5155's ceiling**).

✅ **"Declaring these ten did NOT buy rejection of a misspelling, and the new test pins that explicitly so the card cannot be misread."** That sentence is worth more than the ten declarations: it stops the next reader concluding this surface now rejects typos, and it pins the limit rather than leaving it to prose.

✅ And both halves carry **positive** counter-probes (a well-typed value accepted on every key at runtime; a correctly-typed literal assigning on every key at compile time) — *"without them a declaration narrowed to `never` would satisfy all ten directives."* That is the vacuity hole closed at its root.

### The ablation discipline

✅ Ablation A predicted red on `types` and measured **exactly ten `TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive`**, one per declared key. ✅ And it predicted **green on `plugin-gantt` and said so up front as a non-signal** — because under `BaseSchema`'s index signature a read site **can never be the detector** (`schema.readOnly` type-checks as `any` either way), which is why the pin lives in `packages/types` under `tsconfig.test.json`. ⛔ Declaring a green leg a non-signal *before* running it is what stops it being read as confirmation later.

✅ The rebuild was handled correctly and *proved*: `plugin-gantt` resolves `@object-ui/types` through `exports`→`dist`, so the mutation was rebuilt between edit and reading, **and confirmed to have reached dist** — `grep -c skipWeekends packages/types/dist/objectql.d.ts` went **2 → 0**. ⛔ That is the stale-artifact false green ruled out by measurement rather than by asserting a rebuild happened.

### The three findings, and how #6050 was found

✅ **#6050** — the `plugin-gantt` README's `navigation` example shows `basePath`, which no read site consumes and which the spec's strict six-member `NavigationConfigSchema` **actively rejects**, so the documented snippet fails validation and the `mode: 'page'` it teaches never takes effect. ⭐ **Found because the new pin's first draft used the README's own example verbatim as its well-typed fixture and failed with `unrecognized_keys: ['basePath']`.** Using published documentation as a test fixture is a technique this lane should steal: it makes the docs a checked artifact for free.

✅ **#6051** — `getGanttConfig` reads **24 further** top-level keys that neither `ObjectGanttSchema` nor `ObjectGridSchema` declares, hidden by `BaseSchema`'s index signature rather than by a cast, **so no syntax exists to grep for**. Correctly graded as a *ruling* (is the flat spelling a sanctioned second authoring form for `GanttConfig`?) rather than a mechanical fix.

✅ **#6052** — `String(schema.label)` with `BaseSchema.label: string | I18nLabel` exports an inline locale map as `[object Object]`. Pre-existing, and this PR is **deliberately behaviour-preserving** there — *"dropping the cast only makes the union visible at the call site for the first time."* ✅ Naming that the fix **revealed** it rather than caused it is the accurate framing.
